## findings (r5, frozen pre-reveal)
- T1R4-ACCT closed: no tier discount on the added-names line; account read removed.
- T1R4-SHAPE closed: nm_billing_span tiers are a floor (max), a whole-year step (ceil) and linear proration — distinct shapes; names has an honest method.

- T1R5-EVT — SOURCE-POLICY RED (the r1 EVT-c class again): the tier taken bills 3 name-years when 761 days (2 years and 31 days) remain to the end date 2029-01-07. The extra ~334 days lie past the subscription end, which no certificate can outlast (base ssl_lifecycle_clock: "its last certificate is never valid beyond that date"). The next auto-renew then bills the same name again for those days ("plus additional_name_price_per_year times the extra names times the years"). Base ssl_names_charge: "Names added to a multi-domain certificate mid-term are billed for the remaining subscription"; the tool records period_end = the end date while the amount covers a year beyond it.
- T1R5-COND — SOURCE-POLICY RED (prerequisite_graph check 7; present since r3, missed by this auditor in r3 and r4): the second-key edge to names declares condition "ssl_holdings.extra_names on the sibling has risen by the names the customer says the new server serves beyond those the sibling covers, each carried by an added-names line". In this world 3 of the 4 names are carried by complimentary names (no billing line), so the declared condition stays false after the gold chain while the rule sentence ("every name the new server serves has been added to the sibling certificate") holds. The worklog's round-5 claim that this condition was restated is not reflected in the file (secondkey policy == r4).
